title: Help with consistent narrative generation
author: Warsel77
selftext:
Hi, I banged my head against the following problem for a while now, maybe you have a suggestion:

I am trying to set up a system where an LLM writes a quest overview (text only at this point).  
  
I am aiming for:  
1) respects a (provided) world bible  
2) each step is consistent with the previous  
3) choices need to matter (and similar "playable / fun to play" considerations).  
4) it needs to be game-compatible (some constraints on type of interactions players can take.. combat / dialogue / riddles / exposition).

  
I have tried:  
\+ One-shot generation with a world bible  
\+ Using existing quests from games as structures to re-wire  
\+ Building beat-by-beat (current approach).  
  
One-shotting them and had some limted success with ChatGPT, less so with Deepseek v4 (pro and flash were very similar) and it was most of the time horrible with Claude (Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5).

ChatGPT seems to be most creative but hard to control.

Claude is unable to distinguish internal (non-player-facing) from external (player-facing) information as well as character-owned vs. world-owned perspective.

Referencing existing quest structures did not improve things much. Eg harvesting Witcher and Skyrim quests as a reference model and then scrambling things led to non-workable quests for me.

The quests are RPG-style quests.

Any suggestions what you'd do is appreciated.

comments.author: Ohgood9002
comments.body:
Have you created a "Narrative Design" design document and fed that to your AI agent?

I'd recommend that.

Prompt it something like "we need to work on the narrative design for quests. Ask me 20 questions and use my responses to create a narrative design document to follow for quest creation"

replies.author: Warsel77
replies.body:
Yes, I have created a set of documents including how to use the world info, what to invent and what not to, consistency requirements, scoring using "is it fun" proxies based on a number of articles on quest design / dopamine etc.

So method (how to intake information), craft guide (how to write), quest shapes, revision/critique, output format, verification, reward metrics. Each of these is a separate file creating, more or less, an agent OS.

I will try if the exact prompt keywords "Narrative Design" make a difference though.

replies.author: Ohgood9002
replies.body: Id have to read your documentation to further assist. I dont want to recommend things you have have already done or included

comments.author: PerfectSituation1668
comments.body: You really have to babysit it for every story beat. Also give it a structure to follow. So the skeleton of your story already has to be there if you want to be consistent. They can fill it in if it's there. It's still a machine and machines make dumb mistakes if instructed wrong.

comments.author: RichardTheApe
comments.body:
I think you’re probably spending too much time per token working through a world Bible. Additionally I think reminding the AI of player constraints and mechanics per prompt will yield better responses as well. 

I also think you should give the prompt greater guidance than “create a quest within these very general parameters” 

You should think of a start, twist, and end scenario.

replies.author: Warsel77
replies.body:
I am currently running something like:  
0) write a story seed  
1) create a general outline (hook/line/sinker) in line with the world bible  
2) break into story beats   
3) flesh out beat by beat (already boiled down to relevant world info, not everything)

On the player constraints, yes - I am feeding that there are just 4 interaction types (eg conversation, combat, item use, riddle) and whatever story is written should resonate with one of them.

I take the initial beats from the first step and then, in a second one, formally move it into the quest format - so there is a translation step from prose to structure.

That second part works relatively OK, rarely fails.

The biggest issue is unreliable prose.. eg a character not being able to understand world vs. self knowledge. Claude is the worst at this, Deepseek and ChatGPT are pretty OK. Not exactly sure why. Qwen 3.6-27B is actually, surprisingly, on par with them, very useable.
